solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The best ever Australian or American album

parts.note: the Americas and Australasia are together called the New World, as against Europe's Old World
an album is an LP, a record

explanation.surface: A music critic hails some antipodean or US album as the greatest of all time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about an album, but it splits into a definition and two charade pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A world record is the best performance ever achieved; the fresh one is the latest such peak.

clue.text: Pin-up picture of national leaders of empire

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word pin is read from the bottom, so backwards
the leaders of words are their first letters, taken here from picture, of and national

explanation.surface: A pin-up photo shows the national leaders of some empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like one hyphenated word but splits: 'up' is the reversal signal, which works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan, which was formally styled an empire under its emperors.

clue.text: Right to enter costliest wine order three days before Christmas

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the middle of the rearranged letters, as if entering them
to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders the priciest wine for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges COSTLIEST WINE into WINTESOLSTICE, and 'to enter' puts R inside it after WINTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern year's shortest day falls on or about 21 December, which is three days before the 24th, Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Spiritualism and honour, I see

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
ah is the exclamation of someone who now understands, like I see

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium is awarded an honour and says she understands.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a Caribbean system of folk magic and sorcery, a belief in working with spirits.

clue.text: Devils oddly not into temptation for fun

indicators.note: the kept letters are placed inside the synonym for temptation

parts.note: a lure is a temptation or enticement

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of the word devils leaves only its even ones

explanation.surface: Devils, strangely, do not lead us into temptation just for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly not' means skip the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of Devils and keep the rest; 'into' then sets them inside the temptation word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent on enjoyment, so it stands for fun or recreation.

clue.text: See 1
Previously on holiday here, in French circle by virtue of job

parts.note: ex means former, so previously
someone off work is on holiday
the French word for here is ici
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A former holidaymaker in a French social circle gets in only because of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase is built from four pieces in order; ICI is French for here.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase describes membership or rights held because of an office or position, not personal choice.

clue.text: Switch positions to contain the risk, just in case

indicators.note: the two positions hold the next word inside them

parts.note: a light switch has two positions, on and off
to take a chance is to take a risk

explanation.surface: Flicking a switch to limit the risk, simply as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' gives both settings of a switch at once; 'to contain' then wraps them round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the off chance means doing it in case a slim possibility comes about.

clue.text: Doctor's instruction has carrier admitting refusal to return weapon

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards
the carrier lets the refusal inside it

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
no is a refusal
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A soldier refuses to give back a weapon carried by a porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts NO in HOD, giving HONOD; 'to return' reverses it to DONOH. A hod is a builder's brick trough.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle of avoiding injury to patients is traditionally linked to the Hippocratic oath, a physician's core rule.

clue.text: Dose people gripped by fear of coronavirus?

indicators.note: the people are held inside the word for fear

parts.note: panic is sudden fear
in a stage New York accent, 'dose people' is 'those people', who are 'dem' for 'them'

explanation.surface: People seized by fear of the virus take a dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dose' is not medicine: it mimics the stage Brooklyn 'dese, dem and dose' accent, where those people are 'dem'. 'gripped by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: COVID-19, caused by a coronavirus, was declared a worldwide epidemic in 2020; the question mark marks definition by example.

clue.text: At the end, drugs frequently mollify

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word drugs is kept

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: In the end, frequent drug use calms people down.
explanation.definitionFit: To mollify someone is to soothe or appease them, making their anger less hard.

clue.text: The Financial Times will source properly

definitions.meaning: a newspaper speaks of itself as we
a spring or water source sunk in the ground

explanation.surface: The newspaper promises to find its information correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition; the first relies on a paper's editorial 'we', with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a source of water, and done well means done properly; WE'LL is we will.

clue.text: This party is certainly no closed shop!

definitions.text: This party is certainly no closed shop!

parts.words: This party is certainly no closed shop!
parts.note: a closed shop admits only union members; a gathering where anyone may drop in is the very opposite

explanation.surface: A party that welcomes all comers is the reverse of an exclusive workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is a party or day when anyone may visit freely, unlike a members-only closed shop.

clue.text: New hotel servant sent back

indicators.note: the two pieces are read in reverse order and backwards

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a serf is a feudal servant bound to the land

explanation.surface: A new hotel worker is dismissed and sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses H + SERF, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fresh is newly made or recently arrived, so it is new.

clue.text: Man may be misled when clothing is discarded

indicators.note: removing the clothing of a word strips away its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A man may be led astray once he takes his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man; MISLED loses M and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so it is an example of this word for an island.

clue.text: Quiet time surrounded by deer, dogs and ponies

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the time letter sits inside the deer

parts.note: elands are large African antelope, loosely deer

explanation.surface: A peaceful moment in a field among deer, dogs and ponies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' applies only to the time letter; the quiet sits in front. 'dogs' is part of the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetland sheepdogs (shelties) and Shetland ponies both take their name from the Scottish islands.

clue.text: Hellish master provided in cruel twist

indicators.note: the conditional word goes inside the rearranged letters
a twist rearranges the letters of the word cruel

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A master who turns cruel, with a vicious twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges the letters of cruel into LUCER, and 'in' opens that up after LUC to take the condition word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan, lord of hell.

clue.text: Within campus, deep suspicion rises and accelerates

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom up, so backwards
the letters sit inside the run of clue words campus, deep suspicion

explanation.surface: On a university campus, suspicion grows and quickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' takes PUSDEEPS from 'campus, deep suspicion', and 'rises' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To go faster is to quicken your pace; that phrasal verb is a synonym for accelerates.

clue.text: See 2
Saw spin deliveries start to backfire

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A spin bowler's deliveries begin to go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the old noun for a saying, not the verb. An over is six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a well-worn adage.

clue.text: Little Spar from which many pensioners emerged

parts.note: baby means little, as in a baby grand
a boom is a spar on a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A small boat's spar from which elderly folk climbed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The post-war surge in births produced the generation now reaching retirement and drawing pensions.

clue.text: See 20
Pretentious display of well done party

parts.note: brava is the cry of praise to a female performer, the feminine of bravo
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A showy party congratulating someone on a job well done.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVA is the form of bravo used for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness intended to impress, a swaggering front.

clue.text: See 7
Start a hole to convert tee-shirts into shirts

definitions.meaning: in golf you begin each hole by driving from the tee
taking away the 'tee' from the front of the clothing word leaves plain shirts

explanation.surface: A golfer begins a hole and changes from casual shirts into smart ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as an instruction: tee, off.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers begin each hole with a drive from the teeing ground.

clue.text: Stand 1050

parts.note: read as 10 and 50: the answer to 10 across means ease, and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: '1050' is not a number: it is clue 10 (SOFTEN, a synonym of EASE) followed by 50, Roman L.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's easel is a stand that holds a canvas.

clue.text: Second-rate gardening tools, and another that helps you stop

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
rakes are gardening tools
a hoe is another gardening tool

explanation.surface: Cheap garden tools, and one more to help you halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake shoe is the curved block pressed against a wheel or drum to slow a vehicle.

clue.text: At the end of three months, it glows

indicators.note: only the shared ending of the months is kept, the front of each name dropped

parts.note: September, November and December all end in the same five letters

explanation.surface: After a quarter of a year, something lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: Any of the three months works: NOV or DEC goes as readily as SEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment of coal or wood left in a dying fire.

clue.text: Thin broadcaster coverage of pub

indicators.note: the broadcaster covers, so encloses, the pub

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A thin slice of TV coverage given to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny is an informal synonym for thin, meaning lean or bony.

clue.text: Gaza-born recipe for chickpeas

definitions.note: plural in the clue though the answer is one chickpea; the setter's slip

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients, so the letters of the hyphenated word are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe for chickpeas from someone born in Gaza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' rearranges GAZA-BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The garbanzo bean is the Spanish-derived name, common in America, for the chickpea.

clue.text: I don't care for redundant advice to onanist

definitions.meaning: a shrugging reply meaning do what you like
someone who masturbates hardly needs telling to gratify himself

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a pointless tip given to a self-pleaser.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: an onanist needs no such advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'do as you like' signals indifference to someone's choice.
